extDescription.message: On-device scam & phishing protection: warns you, spots brand look-alikes, checks messages. Nothing leaves your device.

popupPausedSummary.message: Protection is paused — turn it on to resume.

popupNotHttp.message: Browser pages and the web store aren't scanned.

popupDangerSummary.message: Don't enter passwords or card details here.

popupSuspiciousSummary.message: Take care before typing anything here.

copyReportFooter.message: Checked on-device by ScamShield — free, open-source: https://joelstephen97.github.io/scamshield/

checkMessageHint.message: Paste a suspicious SMS, WhatsApp or email text, or a link. Checked entirely on your device.

checkMessagePlaceholder.message: Paste the message or link here…

msgSafe.message: Looks safe — no scam signals found

qrScanTitle.message: Scan this page for QR codes

qrScanHint.message: Decodes QR codes in this page's images and checks where they lead — before you scan them with your phone. Checked entirely on your device.

qrScanNone.message: No QR codes found on this page.

footerTrustLine.message: Made on-device. No data leaves your browser.

takeMeToRealSite.message: Take me to the real site

whatsNewLine1.message: Far fewer warnings: ScamShield now speaks up only when it's confident.

whatsNewLine2.message: Scam links and scam ads are now caught while you scroll.

popupBrandDangerSummary.message: Looks like $BRAND$, but isn't. Don't enter your password here.

popupPrivacyLeakPlain.message: Sent your email/phone to $HOST$ before you submitted.

popupPrivacyLeakHashed.message: Sent your email/phone to $HOST$ (hashed) before you submitted.

popupPrivacyFingerprint.message: $HOST$ is fingerprinting your device to track you.

popupPrivacyNotifyLure.message: This site tried a "click Allow" notification trick.

popupPrivacyCredExfilPassword.message: Sent your password to $HOST$ — a different site than the one you were on.

popupPrivacyCredExfilCard.message: Sent your card details to $HOST$ — a different site than the one you were on.

protectionLead.message: Everything here runs on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere unless you turn on community reporting at the bottom.

protectionOnHint.message: Scans pages for scams and warns you. Turn off to pause everything.

grpScamsHint.message: Blocking known-bad sites and catching new phishing on your device.

grpPopupsHint.message: Fake virus alerts, screen-lockers and clipboard hijacks.

grpShoppingHint.message: Spots fake online shops and where search ads really go.

grpPrivacyHint.message: Catches sites that leak your details or track your device — all on your device.

optBlockKnownHint.message: Stops pages on the daily-updated threat list before they load.

optPageAnalysisHint.message: Reads the page's wording, layout and icons on your device to catch scams that aren't on any list yet.

optClickfixHint.message: Stops pages that tell you to press Win+R and paste a command (ClickFix malware).

optFakeupdateHint.message: Blocks pages pretending your browser needs an update so you download malware.

optHideHint.message: Greys out "you've won a prize" blocks inside otherwise normal pages.

optQrScanHint.message: Decodes QR codes in large images on the page and checks their destination before you scan them with your phone — the on-device counter to "quishing" (QR-code phishing) emails. You can also scan any page on demand from the popup.

optTechscamHint.message: Detects fake "your PC is infected, call this number" pages and gives you a way out.

optClipboardHint.message: Warns when a site secretly puts a command or crypto address on your clipboard.

optShopHint.message: Looks for fake countdowns, fake "only 2 left" pressure, missing contact details and off-platform payment (Zelle/wire/crypto), and shows them in the popup.

optSerpHint.message: On Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo, flags a sponsored result whose ad goes somewhere other than the site it shows, and marks risky results with a small red/amber dot.

optWalletHint.message: Warns before you approve token spends, "Permit" signatures or account delegations that drainers abuse.

optLeakyFormHint.message: Warns when a site sends the email or phone you typed to a tracker before you press submit, or when a form sends a password or card number to a different site than the one you are on.

optFingerprintHint.message: Tells you which script is fingerprinting your device to track you across sites.

optNotifyHint.message: Flags the "click Allow to continue" trick sites use to spam you with pop-ups.

optStrictHint.message: For anyone who wants maximum caution: even "suspicious" pages are blocked with a full-screen warning and simpler wording. Best for helping a less confident family member stay safe.

optReportingHint.message: Sends the site name (never the full address or page text) and anonymous risk signals of pages flagged dangerous, and of sites you report. Off by default.

trustedLead.message: Protection is paused on these sites. Resume one to protect it again.

optTenantApexBadge.message: Covers every site on $APEX$ — remove it and trust the specific site instead

historyLead.message: Stored only on this device (site names, never full addresses).

feedLead.message: A regularly updated list of known scam sites, built from public, licence-vetted phishing and malware lists. ScamShield only downloads it.

backupHint.message: Save your settings and paused sites to a file, or load them on another computer.

syncHint.message: Keep your settings and paused sites in step on every browser where you're signed in. Uses your browser's own sync — ScamShield still has no account or server. Off by default.

optWhatSentBody.message: A report contains only: the site name (hostname), the verdict and internal reason codes, numeric risk signals derived from the address and page layout (hashed word counts and counts of forms, inputs and links — never the text itself), matched brand names, the extension version, and the hour. Never the full address (path or query), page text, anything you typed, cookies, or any identifier of you or your device. Reports are deleted after 180 days.

hotListSub.message: …and the last-48-hour hot list, refreshed hourly.

optFeedUrlHint.message: Point this at your own JSON to self-host, or leave blank to disable updates.

optThemeHint.message: Follow your system, or pick one.

optLangHint.message: Applies to ScamShield's warnings, popup and settings. Syncs with your other devices if sync is on.

supportFreeOnDevice.message: ScamShield is free and runs entirely on your device.

netNoTelemetry.message: ScamShield makes no analytics, telemetry or tracking requests — ever. It only makes the requests listed below, and you can check this yourself: open your browser's DevTools → Network tab, use ScamShield normally, and you will see nothing else.

receiptFeedDetail.message: Public threat-list files: the main list, a small hourly update, and one small detail file if a page matches. Same for everyone; nothing about you or your pages is sent.

receiptReportDetail.message: Only if you turned reporting on. Site name + numeric signals, never URLs or page text.

receiptIconDetail.message: Fetches a page's own favicon to spot brand look-alikes. No third party, no cookies.

optExportSyncHint.message: Settings can be exported/imported below and (optionally) synced across your own devices.

optNothingYetGood.message: Nothing yet — that’s a good thing.

statsRulesActiveHint.message: In force right now, including the list built into ScamShield.

statsFooter.message: Every number is counted on your device. Nothing on this page is sent anywhere.

reviewAskBody.message: ScamShield has now stopped $COUNT$ scams for you. If it's earned it, a short review helps other people find it — it's free and always will be.

bannerDangerBrand.message: Dangerous page — looks like $BRAND$, but isn't

interstitialHead1.message: Stop — this page is trying to scam you

interstitialHead2.message: Hold on — this looks like a scam page

interstitialReassure.message: If you already typed a password or card number on this page, change it now.

techScamBody.message: This is a web page, not your computer — your computer is fine. Real security warnings never lock your screen or show a phone number. Do not call, and do not pay.

walletRiskyBody.message: If you did not expect this, cancel. Drainers use these requests to steal your crypto.

interstitialFallback.message: This page matches the pattern of a known scam.

toastSupportAsk.message: ScamShield just protected you — it’s free and runs on your device. Chip in? ❤

guardFormDestKnown.message: This form sends your password to $DEST$, not to $HOST$. Sending a password to a different website is how scammers steal logins.

guardFormDestUnknown.message: This form sends your password to a different website than the one you are visiting. This is a common way scammers steal logins.

guardWalletCollision.message: ScamShield blocked a wallet request while another warning was open. Close it and retry.

guardWalletFallback.message: This site is requesting a sensitive wallet action.

guardPrivacyFallback.message: A privacy issue was detected on this page.

guardTechScamFallback.message: This page is using scare tactics.

guardClipboardBlockedPayload.message: Blocked by ScamShield — this site put a dangerous command on your clipboard. Do not paste it anywhere.

clipboardNoticeCmdTitle.message: You copied a terminal command from $HOST$

clipboardNoticeCmdBody.message: Only run it if you trust this site. Real sites never ask you to paste commands to "verify" anything.

clipboardNoticeAddrTitle.message: You copied a crypto address from $HOST$

clipboardNoticeAddrBody.message: Check it matches the address you expected before sending anything.

clipboardWarnTitle.message: $HOST$ changed your clipboard on its own

ackMuted.message: ScamShield won't show this warning on $HOST$ again.

dontWarnHere.message: Don't warn me on this site

leakTitle.message: Your details left this page before you pressed Send

credPostTitle.message: This form sends what you type to another site

guardLeakyFormPlain.message: This site sent your email/phone to $HOST$ in plain text — before you pressed submit.

guardLeakyFormHashed.message: This site sent your email/phone to $HOST$ as a hashed ($ALGO$) identifier — before you pressed submit.

guardNotifyLure.message: This site is trying to get notification permission using a "click Allow to continue" trick. You can safely Block it.

serpAdMismatch.message: ⚠ ScamShield: this ad goes to $ACTUAL$, not $SHOWN$

serpBadgeDanger.message: ScamShield: this result is on our threat block list

serpBadgeCaution.message: ScamShield: this result shows scam warning signs

reason_ipHost.message: Uses a raw IP address instead of a domain name.

reason_atSymbol.message: URL contains an "@" that can hide the real destination.

reason_punycodeHost.message: Domain uses punycode, often used to mimic real brands.

reason_idnHomograph.message: This domain imitates "$BRAND$" using look-alike foreign characters.

reason_brandLookalike.message: Domain looks like it impersonates a well-known brand.

reason_suspiciousTld.message: Domain uses a top-level domain frequently abused by scams.

reason_brandFuzzyMatch.message: This domain closely resembles $BRAND$'s real domain — check the address bar carefully before entering anything.

reason_deepSubdomainChain.message: Domain has an unusually deep chain of subdomains below its real domain — a common cloaking trick.

reason_longHostLabel.message: Domain contains an unusually long part, often used to bury a fake brand name or hide the real domain.

reason_shortenerHost.message: This is a link-shortener domain ($HOST$) — the real destination is hidden until you click it.

reason_riskAbusedTld.message: Domain's top-level domain ($TLD$) has a high rate of scam abuse in ScamShield's threat-feed risk tables.

reason_riskDynamicHost.message: Domain is hosted on a dynamic-DNS or free-hosting provider frequently abused for scam pages.

reason_brandForeignSuffix.message: Uses $BRAND$'s name on a .$SUFFIX$ address the real $BRAND$ never uses.

reason_gatewayRedirect.message: This page was reached through a short redirect link on $HOST$ that led to a completely different site — a common scam-gateway pattern.

reason_feedBlock.message: This domain matches ScamShield's threat feed, confirmed by $COUNT$ independent sources.

reason_feedBlockOne.message: This domain matches ScamShield's threat feed, confirmed by $COUNT$ independent source.

reason_feedWarn.message: This domain matches a lower-confidence entry in ScamShield's threat feed ($COUNT$ sources) — proceed carefully.

reason_feedWarnOne.message: This domain matches a lower-confidence entry in ScamShield's threat feed ($COUNT$ source) — proceed carefully.

reason_newDomain.message: Domain appears on a newly-registered-domains list — most scam sites are only days old.

reason_credentialFormForeignDomain.message: A password form on this page sends your credentials to a different site.

reason_crossOriginCredPost.message: This form sends your password or card details to $HOST$ — a different site than the one you are on.

reason_credentialExfilScript.message: This page's code sends what you type to a $SERVICE$ bot, a common way phishing kits steal logins.

reason_credentialExfilBlocked.message: This page tried to send the password you typed to a $SERVICE$ bot. ScamShield blocked it.

reason_hiddenIframes.message: Page contains hidden frames that may capture input.

reason_seedPhraseAsk.message: This page asks for your wallet recovery phrase — never enter it; this steals your funds.

reason_brandImpersonationContent.message: This page looks like "$BRAND$" but is not on its real website.

reason_deliveryFeeScam.message: This page pretends to be $BRAND$ and asks for card details to release a package. Carriers never collect fees through pages like this.

reason_brandIconMismatch.message: This page uses $BRAND$'s icon but is not $BRAND$'s website.

reason_credentialFormOnTenantHost.message: Asks for a password on a shared hosting platform ($HOST$) where anyone can publish a page in seconds.

reason_brandInTenantHost.message: $BRAND$'s name is in the address of a free-hosting page that asks for a password.

reason_contentPhishingPattern.message: Page wording and layout resemble known phishing pages.

reason_techScamPhoneAsk.message: Page urges you to call a phone number for "support" — a hallmark of tech-support scams.

reason_techScamFakeAlert.message: This is a web page pretending to be a system alert — your computer is fine. Real Microsoft/Apple warnings never show phone numbers.

reason_techScamFullscreen.message: Page forced fullscreen to make itself hard to close.

reason_techScamAlarmAudio.message: Page plays alarm audio to panic you.

reason_techScamDialogFlood.message: Page spammed pop-up dialogs to trap you.

reason_techScamHistoryTrap.message: Page is hijacking your Back button.

reason_walletBlindSign.message: A site asked your wallet to blind-sign arbitrary data — a common drainer trick.

reason_walletPermitApproval.message: This signature is a token approval ("Permit"). Signing it lets this site move your tokens or NFTs later, without asking you again — the most common wallet-drainer signature.

reason_walletDelegation7702.message: This transaction would hand control of your account to a contract (EIP-7702 delegation) — a technique drainers use to empty wallets.

reason_walletSetApprovalAll.message: This transaction grants a site control over ALL your NFTs in a collection.

reason_walletUnlimitedApprove.message: This transaction gives a site UNLIMITED permission to spend your tokens.

reason_walletTokenApprove.message: This transaction lets a site spend some of your tokens.

reason_clickfixPasteRun.message: This page put a system command on your clipboard and is telling you to paste and run it. Real websites never do this — running it would infect your computer.

reason_clickfixFakeCaptcha.message: This "verification" asks you to press Win+R and paste a command. Real CAPTCHAs never ask you to run anything — this installs malware.

reason_clickfixWinR.message: This page instructs you to open the Windows Run box and paste something — a pattern used to trick people into running malware.

reason_clickfixCaptchaDisguise.message: The instructions are disguised as a human-verification step.

reason_clipboardCommand.message: A site copied a system command to your clipboard. Do NOT paste it into a terminal or the Run box.

reason_clipboardCryptoAddress.message: A site put a cryptocurrency address on your clipboard — verify it before pasting.

reason_fakeUpdatePrompt.message: This page pretends your browser needs an update and offers a download. Real update prompts come from the browser itself — never from a web page. The download is very likely malware.

reason_msgOtpAsk.message: Asks you to share an OTP, PIN, or password — no legitimate service ever does this.

reason_msgUrgencyDeadline.message: Adds pressure with an artificial deadline — a classic scam tactic.

reason_qrCodeDestination.message: This page contains a QR code pointing to $URL$ — checked automatically before you scan it with your phone.

reason_shop_countdownReset_detail.message: A "hurry, offer ends" timer resets every visit — the urgency is fake.

reason_shop_offPlatformPay_detail.message: Checkout pushes you to Zelle/Venmo/CashApp/wire/crypto — you cannot get this money back if it is a scam.

reason_shop_fakeScarcity_detail.message: Injected "only a few left / N people viewing" pressure widgets.

reason_shop_badgeHotlink_detail.message: A "secure"/"verified" badge that is just an image, linking nowhere.

reason_shop_missingContact_detail.message: No real address, phone or company details — normal for a throwaway scam shop.

obLead.message: It watches the pages you visit and warns you about scams — entirely on your device. Your browsing never leaves your computer.

obPinBody.message: Click the puzzle-piece icon in your toolbar, then the pin next to ScamShield, so you can see each page's status at a glance.

blockedLead.message: $HOST$ is on ScamShield's list of known scam and malicious sites, so the page was stopped before it could load. Nothing ran and nothing you typed was sent.

blockedLeadHot.message: $HOST$ was reported for phishing in the last two days, so the page was stopped before it could load. Nothing ran and nothing you typed was sent.

blockedListedGeneric.message: Listed in ScamShield's block list of confirmed scam domains.

blockedTrustSite.message: Not a scam? Trust this site

blockedVisitHint.message: Opens the site with ScamShield paused on it for 1 hour.

blockedFooter.message: Blocked on your device. Nothing about this page was sent anywhere.

continuePausesHour.message: Pauses ScamShield on this site for 1 hour.

obNote.message: ScamShield is free. Optional: in Settings you can help make it smarter by sharing anonymous reports of scams it catches — it's off unless you turn it on. If it helps you, you can support development from the Settings page.

optHotRejected.message: Latest hot-list update was rejected as unsafe; still using the previous list.

interstitialFooter.message: ScamShield checked this page on your device.

reason_newDomainUnvisited.message: Domain appears on a newly-registered-domains list — most scam sites are only days old, and you have never visited it before.

continueOnce.message: Continues to this page once. ScamShield stays on.

frameFormBlocked.message: ScamShield blocked a sign-in form inside an embedded frame because it sends your password to another site

linkConfirmBlock.message: This link goes to a site on ScamShield's block list

popupBlockedToast.message: ScamShield stopped this page from opening a blocked site

popunderBlockedToast.message: ScamShield stopped this page from opening a new window

popupCantCheckHint.message: ScamShield can't read this page. Browser pages, the web store and PDFs aren't scanned.

popupQuietSummary.message: A few unusual signs — not enough to warn you

popupFineConfirm.message: Trust $HOST$ and stop warning about it?

optLinkGuardHint.message: Tags links that lead to known scam sites and asks before opening them.

optAdGuardHint.message: Collapses ads that lead to known scam sites.

optQuietSitesHint.message: You dismissed warnings on these sites, so ScamShield stays quiet there for a while. Remove one to hear from it again.

surfacesLead.message: Every warning or notice ScamShield put on a page, newest first. Stored only on this device.

blockedLeadEscalated.message: ScamShield closed this page because it kept hiding the warning.

obS1Body.message: Here is what a ScamShield warning looks like, on a pretend sign-in page. Nothing real is opened.

obS2Title.message: Why it needs access to your sites

obS2Body.message: Your browser words this permission as “read and change all your data on all websites”. ScamShield needs it to look at the page you are on and warn you before you type. Every check runs on your device, and nothing leaves your browser unless you choose to share a report in Settings.

demoLabel.message: This is what a warning looks like

demoSub.message: A pretend page. Nothing here is real, and no site is opened.

gbPick.message: Why did you remove it? Pick one, it takes a second.

gbCopied.message: Copied a short note to your clipboard. Nothing was sent. If you want to say more, paste it into a GitHub issue.

gbStatic.message: This page is static: no account, no analytics, and nothing is sent from here. Everything ScamShield stored lived in your browser and went with it.

demoRescue.message: Back to setup (this is a demo)
